question: Some of Swami Dayanand’s followers started a network of schools and colleges called D.A.V. What does ‘A’ stand for in D.A.V.?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Anglo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Dayanand Anglo Vedic (DAV) Trust and Management Society** was founded in **1886 **to fulfil the visionary ideals of the eminent philosopher **Maharishi Dayanand Saraswati**.
 
• It was officially registered under the **Societies Act of 1860.**
 
• The inaugural DAV School was established in Lahore during the same year, with Mahatma Hansraj serving as the Honorary Headmaster.
 
• The DAV family encompasses 900 schools, 75 colleges, and a university.
 
• The "DAV Movement," initiated in 1886 by Lala Lajpat Rai (acknowledged as the Father of the DAV Movement), gained significant traction thanks to the dedicated efforts of individuals such as Mahatma Hans Raj, Pandit Gurudutt Vidyarthi, and numerous other committed Arya Samaj activists. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dayanand Saraswati,** a Hindu philosopher and social leader, is renowned as the founder of the Arya Samaj, a reform movement within Hinduism.
 
• His seminal work,** "Satyarth Prakash," **stands as a significant text elucidating Vedic philosophy and delineating human responsibilities.
 
• In 1876, he issued a groundbreaking call for Swaraj, advocating "India for Indians," a sentiment later echoed by Lokmanya Tilak. Rejecting idolatry and ritualistic practices, he aimed to revive the pure ideologies of the Vedas.
 
• Esteemed figures such as philosopher and former President of India, S. Radhakrishnan, along with Sri Aurobindo, recognized him as one of the key architects of Modern India.
